reviews.text: I had to take my pet to an emergency vet overnight from Sunday to Saturday and was promptly attended to. Everything was fine and okay.

My experience with Cetravet was simply TERRIBLE and terrifying. If I could give zero stars, I would.

I took my dog, Mel, to be seen and received a diagnosis that she had a serious hip problem. Based on this diagnosis, extremely strong medications were prescribed, including morphine and its derivatives, which she started taking because, obviously, we trusted the assessment of a veterinary professional.

The problem is that, later, we discovered that Mel's hip was perfect. In other words: in our experience, she received a diagnosis that did not correspond to the real situation and was subjected to very strong medications that she didn't need to be taking.

And the consequences were very serious.

After that, Mel suffered an extremely severe kidney crisis, with drastic changes in her tests, and even risked her life. It was heartbreaking to watch an animal that went in to be treated for a supposed problem come out of all that situation in an infinitely more worrying state.

Luckily, we sought help at the DOC Veterinary Hospital, where Mel received different treatment and her life was saved. It was only then that we were able to understand the seriousness of what was happening and also that the diagnosis related to her hip didn't make sense given her tests.

It's infuriating because we're talking about lives. Our animals aren't objects on which you can simply test a hypothesis, prescribe extremely strong medications, and then move on if something goes wrong. They are members of our family, some of the most precious beings we have, and they depend completely on the decisions made by the professionals responsible for their care.

After what we experienced, I would never again entrust the life of one of my animals to Cetravet and I wouldn't recommend this service to anyone. The least one expects from a veterinary clinic is caution, responsibility, and safety before prescribing such strong medications, especially when the consequences of a mistake can be so serious.

Mel almost lost her life. We went through days of fear and despair that could have ended in the worst possible way.

I'm leaving this review because I REALLY wish I had found a review like this before taking my dog ​​there. If you love your pet and are thinking about going to Cetravet, I strongly recommend seeking a second opinion before starting any treatment or high-potency medication.

After everything that happened with Mel, our trust in the clinic and, particularly, in the care of the doctor in question was completely destroyed. An experience that I sincerely hope no other family has to go through.

Yesterday I lost my little dog that we rescued from the street at CETRAVET Recreio. It was devastating. After a spaying on May 27th at another clinic in CAVRIO with Dr. Aline Balod Lobão, my dog ​​was lethargic and vomiting. So we rushed there on May 2nd and were seen by Dr. Adriana, who administered Serenia for vomiting and a subcutaneous antibiotic called Convenia. I asked if hospitalization wasn't necessary and if the antibiotic wouldn't have side effects because the poor thing was very fragile. The doctor said there was no need for hospitalization because she was fine. The following day (yesterday) the dog died. She was a being of light! Very cheerful, loving, and obedient. She brought so much joy to our home. We are all devastated. I think there should have been more care. The doctor who performed the spaying blames Dr. Abriana for the antibiotic, and Cetavet says they acted correctly. I don't know who to blame, but I think there was negligence on both sides.

On June 3rd, 2025, our son was seen by Dr. Amanda Mendonça de Melo because he was unable to walk, with his hindquarters sagging. Without knowing his history and without ordering any tests beyond a simple X-ray, she sold him Librela injections. This was an innovative and miraculous medication that was supposedly making dogs with dysplasia rejuvenate by 10 years. In desperation and trusting the professional, we accepted. Bob had an allergic reaction 30 minutes later. Just 5 days later, Bob was hospitalized with insulinoma, pancreatic cancer. ONE MONTH LATER HE DIED.
SEARCH FOR VICTIMS OF LIBRELA ON FACEBOOK AND YOU WILL DISCOVER WHY THIS MEDICATION SHOULD NOT BE SOLD TO ANY PATIENT WITHOUT A THOROUGH EVALUATION BEFOREHAND AND NOT BY ANY VETERINARIAN.
